title: Find the classroom, not the pool
setup: Read a campus information card and a visitor’s question. The floor and the landmark both matter.

lines.speaker: Campus card
lines.text: 這棟大樓在圖書館旁邊，不在宿舍旁邊。
lines.pinyin: Zhè dòng dàlóu zài túshūguǎn pángbiān, bú zài sùshè pángbiān.
lines.translation: This building is beside the library, not beside the dormitory.
lines.note: 棟 counts an entire building. The two location clauses distinguish the correct landmark from a plausible but wrong one.

lines.speaker: Campus card
lines.text: 中文教室在三樓，英文教室在二樓。
lines.pinyin: Zhōngwén jiàoshì zài sān lóu, Yīngwén jiàoshì zài èr lóu.
lines.translation: The Chinese classroom is on the third floor; the English classroom is on the second.
lines.note: Floor numbers come directly before 樓. Keep each subject with its own floor rather than treating the two rooms as one place.

lines.speaker: Campus card
lines.text: 中文老師也在三樓，現在在教室裡面。
lines.pinyin: Zhōngwén lǎoshī yě zài sān lóu, xiànzài zài jiàoshì lǐmiàn.
lines.translation: The Chinese teacher is also on the third floor, inside the classroom now.
lines.note: 也 adds the teacher to the location already established for Chinese class. 現在 describes current whereabouts, not a permanent room assignment.

lines.speaker: Campus card
lines.text: 大樓前面有一家商店，後面有游泳池。
lines.pinyin: Dàlóu qiánmiàn yǒu yì jiā shāngdiàn, hòumiàn yǒu yóuyǒngchí.
lines.translation: There is a shop in front of the building and a swimming pool behind it.
lines.note: The building remains the reference landmark in both clauses. 前面 and 後面 identify opposite sides, not different floors.

lines.speaker: Campus card
lines.text: 商店裡面有茶和咖啡，也有包子。
lines.pinyin: Shāngdiàn lǐmiàn yǒu chá hé kāfēi, yě yǒu bāozi.
lines.translation: Inside the shop there are tea, coffee and buns.
lines.note: 裡面 now refers to the shop rather than the classroom building. 有 lists what is available without saying anything about prices.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.text: 我現在在游泳池旁邊。中文教室在這裡嗎？
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài zài yóuyǒngchí pángbiān. Zhōngwén jiàoshì zài zhèlǐ ma?
lines.translation: I’m beside the pool now. Is the Chinese classroom here?
lines.note: The visitor gives a current location, then asks a question. Do not mistake that question for a correct statement about the classroom.

lines.speaker: Reply
lines.text: 不是在這裡，是在圖書館旁邊的大樓三樓。
lines.pinyin: Bú shì zài zhèlǐ, shì zài túshūguǎn pángbiān de dàlóu sān lóu.
lines.translation: Not here—it’s on the third floor of the building beside the library.
lines.note: 不是…是… corrects the assumption. The location modifier identifies the building first; 三樓 then identifies the floor inside it.

lines.speaker: Reply
lines.text: 你的朋友也在那裡上課。歡迎你來！
lines.pinyin: Nǐ de péngyǒu yě zài nàlǐ shàngkè. Huānyíng nǐ lái!
lines.translation: Your friend also has class there. You’re welcome to come!
lines.note: 那裡 refers back to the classroom just located, not the pool. 在…上課 places the activity at that already-established location.

questions.prompt: Where should the visitor look for the Chinese classroom?
options: Third floor of the building beside the library
questions.explanation: The card and correction agree: choose the library-side building, then its third floor.

questions.prompt: Which place is on the opposite side of the building from the shop?
questions.explanation: The shop is in front and the pool behind. Both positions use the same building as their landmark.

questions.prompt: What does “there” in the final reply point back to?
questions.explanation: The reply first identifies the correct classroom; the following 那裡 refers to that location.

questions.prompt: What information is NOT provided by the card?
questions.explanation: The card lists buns inside the shop but gives no price. Location and availability do not imply a cost.

tips: Follow the reference landmark each time you see front, back or beside.
Read a correction as a replacement for the mistaken claim, not as a second equally valid location.
grammarFocus: Use a landmark as the reference

title: Is there time before calligraphy?
setup: Read Mei’s afternoon schedule and the messages below it. Find a meeting time that fits, without assuming permission has been granted.

lines.text: 從中午十二點到十二點半，我和朋友吃午餐。
lines.pinyin: Cóng zhōngwǔ shí’èr diǎn dào shí’èr diǎn bàn, wǒ hé péngyǒu chī wǔcān.
lines.translation: From noon to twelve thirty, I have lunch with a friend.
lines.note: 從…到… marks the two ends of a time range. 半 means half past the stated hour, not half of the whole lunch period.

lines.text: 下午一點有中文課，兩點半下課。
lines.pinyin: Xiàwǔ yì diǎn yǒu Zhōngwén kè, liǎng diǎn bàn xiàkè.
lines.translation: Chinese class is at one in the afternoon; it finishes at two thirty.
lines.note: The second time is the end of Chinese class. 一點 is a clock reading here, not the later quantity expression meaning a little.

lines.text: 書法課三點開始，四點結束。
lines.pinyin: Shūfǎ kè sān diǎn kāishǐ, sì diǎn jiéshù.
lines.translation: Calligraphy class starts at three and ends at four.
lines.note: 開始 and 結束 label the two boundaries explicitly. This leaves a gap after Chinese class rather than two overlapping classes.

lines.speaker: After 16:00
lines.text: 四點我有事，不能和你見面。
lines.pinyin: Sì diǎn wǒ yǒushì, bù néng hé nǐ jiànmiàn.
lines.translation: I have something to do at four and can’t meet you then.
lines.note: 有事 says the speaker is occupied without naming the task. The end of a class does not automatically mean the person is free.

lines.speaker: Lin · message
lines.text: 兩點四十分在教室外面見面，好不好？
lines.pinyin: Liǎng diǎn sìshí fēn zài jiàoshì wàimiàn jiànmiàn, hǎo bù hǎo?
lines.translation: Shall we meet outside the classroom at two forty?
lines.note: Time comes before place and the meeting action. Forty minutes past two falls after the first class and before the next one.

lines.speaker: Mei · reply
lines.text: 沒問題。三點我有書法課。
lines.pinyin: Méi wèntí. Sān diǎn wǒ yǒu shūfǎ kè.
lines.translation: No problem. I have calligraphy at three.
lines.note: 沒問題 accepts the proposed meeting. The following reminder limits the available time; it does not cancel the acceptance.

lines.speaker: Lin · message
lines.text: 書法很有意思。我可不可以去看你寫字？
lines.pinyin: Shūfǎ hěn yǒuyìsi. Wǒ kě bù kěyǐ qù kàn nǐ xiězì?
lines.translation: Calligraphy is interesting. May I come watch you write?
lines.note: 可不可以 asks permission rather than physical ability. Interest in the class alone does not authorize a visit.

lines.speaker: Mei · reply
lines.text: 等一下，我問老師。
lines.pinyin: Děng yíxià, wǒ wèn lǎoshī.
lines.translation: Wait a moment; I’ll ask the teacher.
lines.note: Mei postpones the answer and names whom she will ask. This is neither a refusal nor confirmation that Lin may enter the class.

questions.prompt: Which suggested time fits between the two classes?
questions.explanation: Chinese ends at 14:30 and calligraphy starts at 15:00. The proposed 14:40 meeting lies inside that gap.

questions.prompt: How much time is there from the agreed meeting to calligraphy?
questions.explanation: They agree on 14:40; calligraphy begins at 15:00, leaving twenty minutes.

questions.prompt: Can Lin definitely attend the calligraphy class?
options: Yes, Mei has already obtained permission
Not yet established; Mei will ask the teacher
questions.explanation: Lin asks permission and Mei says she will ask the teacher. The teacher’s answer is not in the passage.

questions.prompt: Why not simply meet at four?
options: Mei says she has something to do
questions.explanation: The schedule explicitly says Mei is occupied at four, even though calligraphy has ended.

tips: Compare the end of one event with the start of the next, then check notes for extra restrictions.
A request and a promise to ask are not the same as permission.
grammarFocus: Tell clock time with 點 and 分
Mark a range with 從…到…

一點.note: The already-taught clock use of 點, not the later quantity expression.

title: The Saturday plan changes
setup: Read a LINE-style exchange about a day off. Separate the first idea from the plan both people finally accept.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 這個星期六放假，你打算做什麼？
lines.pinyin: Zhè ge xīngqíliù fàngjià, nǐ dǎsuàn zuò shénme?
lines.translation: We have this Saturday off. What are you planning to do?
lines.note: 打算 introduces an intention, not a completed event. The calendar expression sets the day for the whole exchange.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 我想跟你坐火車出去玩。早上去，怎麼樣？
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ zuò huǒchē chūqù wán. Zǎoshang qù, zěnmeyàng?
lines.translation: I’d like to take a train trip with you. How about going in the morning?
lines.note: 跟 introduces a companion and 坐 names the transport. 怎麼樣 invites a reaction, so this first plan remains open to change.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 早上不行，我要做功課。大概中午有空。
lines.pinyin: Zǎoshang bùxíng, wǒ yào zuò gōngkè. Dàgài zhōngwǔ yǒukòng.
lines.translation: Morning won’t work; I need to do homework. I’ll probably be free around noon.
lines.note: 不行 rejects feasibility rather than granting or refusing permission. 大概 makes the free time approximate, not an exact appointment.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 那我們下午去附近的地方吧。
lines.pinyin: Nà wǒmen xiàwǔ qù fùjìn de dìfang ba.
lines.translation: Then let’s go somewhere nearby in the afternoon.
lines.note: 那 connects a response to the obstacle just mentioned. The new proposal changes both timing and the kind of outing.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 學校附近有一家有名的餐廳，我們去吃飯吧。
lines.pinyin: Xuéxiào fùjìn yǒu yì jiā yǒumíng de cāntīng, wǒmen qù chīfàn ba.
lines.translation: There’s a famous restaurant near school. Let’s eat there.
lines.note: A place-first 有 sentence introduces the restaurant. The following suggestion makes the nearby destination concrete.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 坐捷運還是坐公車？捷運比公車快。
lines.pinyin: Zuò jiéyùn háishì zuò gōngchē? Jiéyùn bǐ gōngchē kuài.
lines.translation: Metro or bus? The metro is faster than the bus.
lines.note: 還是 asks the choice; 比 supplies one reason to favor the metro. Faster does not imply cheaper, which the passage never compares.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 好，我們坐捷運。下午兩點在學校外面見面。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒmen zuò jiéyùn. Xiàwǔ liǎng diǎn zài xuéxiào wàimiàn jiànmiàn.
lines.translation: Okay, let’s take the metro. Meet outside the school at two in the afternoon.
lines.note: The acceptance selects the metro and gives a precise time and meeting place, replacing the earlier approximate noon availability.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 沒問題！晚上我想在家看電視。
lines.pinyin: Méi wèntí! Wǎnshang wǒ xiǎng zài jiā kàn diànshì.
lines.translation: No problem! In the evening I want to watch television at home.
lines.note: 沒問題 confirms the meeting. The separate evening intention belongs to Mei and does not say Lin will watch television too.

questions.prompt: Which plan do they finally agree on?
options: An afternoon restaurant outing by metro
questions.explanation: The restaurant replaces the train-trip idea; they choose the metro and confirm the afternoon meeting.

questions.prompt: Why is the morning idea dropped?
questions.explanation: Lin explicitly says morning is not feasible because of homework. No transport failure is mentioned.

questions.prompt: When and where is their confirmed meeting?
questions.explanation: Lin proposes a specific two o’clock meeting outside the school, and Mei accepts in the next message.

questions.prompt: What is said only about Mei’s evening?
options: She wants to watch television at home
She will eat with the whole class
questions.explanation: The evening sentence has Mei as its speaker and subject. It does not extend that plan to both people.

tips: Track revisions: the first proposed transport and time may not survive to the accepted plan.
Approximate availability and a confirmed meeting time serve different purposes.
grammarFocus: State a plan with 打算
Reject an unworkable plan with 不行

title: Two dates, one visiting friend
setup: Read a short visit itinerary and its conditions. A date tells you when; the notes tell you whether the plan is definite.

lines.speaker: 5/6 · arrival
lines.text: 我的朋友五月六號來，要在這裡玩三天。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ de péngyǒu wǔ yuè liù hào lái, yào zài zhèlǐ wán sān tiān.
lines.translation: My friend comes on May sixth and will spend three days here visiting.
lines.note: 五月六號 is a date before the action. 三天 follows 玩 to give the duration of the visit rather than another calendar date.

lines.speaker: 5/6 · afternoon
lines.text: 下午我們打算到學校附近吃飯。
lines.pinyin: Xiàwǔ wǒmen dǎsuàn dào xuéxiào fùjìn chīfàn.
lines.translation: In the afternoon we plan to eat near the school.
lines.note: 打算 labels an intention and 到 introduces the destination. The date is inherited from this part of the itinerary.

lines.speaker: 5/6 · evening
lines.text: 晚上要是他有空，我們就去逛夜市。
lines.pinyin: Wǎnshang yàoshi tā yǒukòng, wǒmen jiù qù guàng yèshì.
lines.translation: If he is free in the evening, we’ll visit the night market.
lines.note: 要是 states a condition and 就 its consequence. The evening outing is not guaranteed merely because it appears on the itinerary.

lines.speaker: 5/7 · morning
lines.text: 七號早上我有中文課，他自己去買水果。
lines.pinyin: Qī hào zǎoshang wǒ yǒu Zhōngwén kè, tā zìjǐ qù mǎi shuǐguǒ.
lines.translation: On the morning of the seventh I have Chinese class; he will buy fruit by himself.
lines.note: The month is understood from the previous date. 自己 makes clear the friend’s errand is separate from the narrator’s class.

lines.speaker: 5/7 · afternoon
lines.text: 下午我們想去貓空。聽說那裡的茶館很有名。
lines.pinyin: Xiàwǔ wǒmen xiǎng qù Māokōng. Tīngshuō nàlǐ de cháguǎn hěn yǒumíng.
lines.translation: In the afternoon we want to go to Maokong. I hear the tea houses there are famous.
lines.note: 聽說 presents reported information that motivates the visit. 那裡 refers to Maokong, not the school mentioned in the previous day’s meal plan.

lines.speaker: Travel note
lines.text: 要是坐公車去，大概要一個鐘頭。
lines.pinyin: Yàoshi zuò gōngchē qù, dàgài yào yí ge zhōngtóu.
lines.translation: If we go by bus, it will probably take one hour.
lines.note: The condition concerns the travel method. 一個鐘頭 is an estimated duration, and 大概 prevents treating it as an exact guaranteed travel time.

lines.speaker: Travel note
lines.text: 要是他不想去貓空，我們就在附近喝茶。
lines.pinyin: Yàoshi tā bù xiǎng qù Māokōng, wǒmen jiù zài fùjìn hē chá.
lines.translation: If he doesn’t want to go to Maokong, we’ll drink tea nearby.
lines.note: The condition gives an alternative based on the friend’s preference. It does not say that he has already refused Maokong.

lines.speaker: Gift note
lines.text: 他說要買水果給我。我喜歡又香又甜的水果。
lines.pinyin: Tā shuō yào mǎi shuǐguǒ gěi wǒ. Wǒ xǐhuān yòu xiāng yòu tián de shuǐguǒ.
lines.translation: He says he wants to buy fruit for me. I like fruit that is fragrant and sweet.
lines.note: 給 introduces the recipient of the planned fruit purchase. 又…又… joins two qualities; neither clause names a specific fruit variety.

questions.prompt: Which activity depends on the friend being free?
options: Visiting the night market on the sixth
questions.explanation: The night-market line explicitly starts a condition with 要是他有空. It is not an unconditional appointment.

questions.prompt: Who buys fruit while the narrator is in class?
questions.explanation: The line contrasts the narrator’s class with 他自己去買水果, assigning the errand to the friend.

questions.prompt: What happens if the friend does not want to visit Maokong?
questions.explanation: The alternative clause explicitly pairs not wanting Maokong with drinking tea in the nearby area.

questions.prompt: Which statement distinguishes the two time expressions correctly?
options: May sixth is the length of the stay
May sixth is arrival; three days is the stay length
Three days means arriving on May third
The bus trip lasts three days
questions.explanation: The date gives arrival, the duration gives the stay, and the separate bus note gives an estimated hour of travel.

tips: Separate unconditional entries from entries introduced by “if.”
A calendar date, a visit duration and an estimated journey length answer different questions.
grammarFocus: Condition and consequence with 要是…就…
Say how long with a duration after the verb
Mark the time of an event with …的時候

title: A room beside the library
setup: A landlord’s short listing and viewing instructions. Match the room’s facilities to the route and meeting details.

lines.speaker: Listing
lines.text: 圖書館旁邊的大樓有一間空房間，在三樓。
lines.pinyin: Túshūguǎn pángbiān de dàlóu yǒu yì jiān kōng fángjiān, zài sān lóu.
lines.translation: The building beside the library has a vacant room on the third floor.
lines.note: 旁邊的大樓 identifies which building; 三樓 identifies the floor. 間 counts rooms, while 空 describes availability.

lines.speaker: Listing
lines.text: 這間是套房，有浴室，沒有廚房。
lines.pinyin: Zhè jiān shì tàofáng, yǒu yùshì, méiyǒu chúfáng.
lines.translation: It is a studio room with a bathroom but no kitchen.
lines.note: 有 and 沒有 distinguish an included facility from a missing one. Do not assume a kitchen just because the room is self-contained.

lines.speaker: Layout
lines.text: 浴室在右邊，窗戶在左邊。房間很乾淨。
lines.pinyin: Yùshì zài yòubiān, chuānghù zài zuǒbiān. Fángjiān hěn gānjìng.
lines.translation: The bathroom is on the right, the window on the left. The room is clean.
lines.note: The two sides refer to the room’s described layout. 乾淨 is a separate assessment of condition, not another location.

lines.speaker: Nearby
lines.text: 樓下有超市，附近也有餐廳。
lines.pinyin: Lóuxià yǒu chāoshì, fùjìn yě yǒu cāntīng.
lines.translation: There is a supermarket downstairs and there are also restaurants nearby.
lines.note: 樓下 and 附近 are different location scopes. The restaurants are nearby; the text does not place all of them downstairs.

lines.speaker: Travel
lines.text: 從這裡到學校，走路五分鐘就到了。
lines.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ dào xuéxiào, zǒulù wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
lines.translation: From here to school, it is only a five-minute walk.
lines.note: 從…到… sets a route. 就 presents arrival as quick or easy; the five-minute figure belongs to walking, not to a bus journey.

lines.speaker: Viewing
lines.text: 你可以星期六下午來看房間。
lines.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ xīngqíliù xiàwǔ lái kàn fángjiān.
lines.translation: You can come see the room on Saturday afternoon.
lines.note: 來看房間 states the purpose of coming. This is an invitation to view, not evidence that a rental agreement already exists.

lines.speaker: Viewing
lines.text: 星期六下午我在樓下。你可以來找我。
lines.pinyin: Xīngqíliù xiàwǔ wǒ zài lóuxià. Nǐ kěyǐ lái zhǎo wǒ.
lines.translation: I’ll be downstairs on Saturday afternoon. You can come find me.
lines.note: The landlord states a location for the viewing time. 來找我 invites the visitor to meet there, distinct from the room’s third-floor location.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.text: 我喜歡自己做飯。這間沒有廚房，我想再看看。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān zìjǐ zuòfàn. Zhè jiān méiyǒu chúfáng, wǒ xiǎng zài kànkan.
lines.translation: I like cooking for myself. This room has no kitchen; I’d like to look some more.
lines.note: The visitor relates the missing facility to a personal preference. 再看看 leaves the decision open rather than confirming a rental.

questions.prompt: Which facility is in the room?
questions.explanation: The room includes a bathroom and explicitly lacks a kitchen. The supermarket and restaurants are separate nearby facilities.

questions.prompt: Where can the visitor find the landlord?
questions.explanation: The landlord says they will be downstairs and invites the visitor to come there, even though the vacant room is on the third floor.

questions.prompt: What is the visitor’s main reservation?
options: There is no kitchen for cooking
The school is an hour away
questions.explanation: The visitor likes cooking and explicitly connects hesitation to the missing kitchen.

questions.prompt: What does the five-minute estimate describe?
options: Walking from the building to school
questions.explanation: The route names the building and school, and 走路 identifies the method as walking.

tips: Do not merge the room’s facilities with amenities elsewhere in the building or neighborhood.
A viewing arrangement is not a decision to rent.
grammarFocus: Use a whole clause to identify a noun

分鐘.note: Reading support for the duration expression already used in the Unit 32 walking example; not a new practice target.

title: Who pays, and what comes next?
setup: Two friends discuss a study plan in a LINE-style chat. Keep past payment, current study and future hopes separate.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 你在臺灣打算念多久的書？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ zài Táiwān dǎsuàn niàn duōjiǔ de shū?
lines.translation: How long are you planning to study in Taiwan?
lines.note: 多久 asks for duration, not a calendar date. 念多久的書 is the taught pattern that places the study duration inside the phrase.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 我計畫先在語言中心念一年中文，再念大學。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ jìhuà xiān zài yǔyán zhōngxīn niàn yì nián Zhōngwén, zài niàn dàxué.
lines.translation: I plan to study Chinese at the language center for a year first, then attend university.
lines.note: 先…再… gives the sequence. The stated year belongs to Chinese study; it does not give the total length of university study.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 學費是你自己付的嗎？
lines.pinyin: Xuéfèi shì nǐ zìjǐ fù de ma?
lines.translation: Was it you who paid the tuition yourself?
lines.note: 是…的 focuses on who paid a known expense. The question seeks a detail of the payment rather than asking what the tuition costs.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 不是我自己付的，是公司替我付的。
lines.pinyin: Bú shì wǒ zìjǐ fù de, shì gōngsī tì wǒ fù de.
lines.translation: I didn’t pay it myself; the company paid it for me.
lines.note: The correction replaces the assumed payer. 替我 means on my behalf, making the company the payer and Mei the beneficiary.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 你也有獎學金嗎？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ yě yǒu jiǎngxuéjīn ma?
lines.translation: Do you also have a scholarship?
lines.note: 也 asks about a possible additional source of support. This question does not establish that a scholarship actually exists.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 沒有。我希望以後在這家公司上班。
lines.pinyin: Méiyǒu. Wǒ xīwàng yǐhòu zài zhè jiā gōngsī shàngbān.
lines.translation: No. I hope to work at this company in the future.
lines.note: 沒有 answers the scholarship question. 希望 marks a hope, so future employment must not be treated as a current job or guaranteed offer.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 你每天念書，累不累？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ měitiān niànshū, lèi bú lèi?
lines.translation: You study every day. Is it tiring?
lines.note: 每天 describes frequency and 累不累 asks about the resulting feeling. This line adds no new source of money or work arrangement.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 有一點累，可是我喜歡學中文。我希望成績好。
lines.pinyin: Yǒuyìdiǎn lèi, kěshì wǒ xǐhuān xué Zhōngwén. Wǒ xīwàng chéngjī hǎo.
lines.translation: A little tiring, but I like learning Chinese. I hope to get good grades.
lines.note: 有一點 gives a mild negative assessment. 可是 contrasts that difficulty with enjoyment; the grades remain a hoped-for result.

questions.prompt: What is the planned study order?
options: Chinese for a year, then university
A year at university, then stop
questions.explanation: 先 identifies Chinese study as the first stage and 再 introduces university afterward.

questions.prompt: Who paid the tuition?
questions.explanation: Mei explicitly corrects the assumption that she paid it herself and names the company as payer.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a hope rather than an established fact?
options: Mei will work at that company
questions.explanation: Mei uses 希望 for future employment. Payment by the company does not by itself establish a job offer.

questions.prompt: How does Mei describe studying?
questions.explanation: Mei combines slight tiredness with liking Chinese, rather than choosing only a positive or negative description.

tips: Separate who performed an action from who benefited from it.
Hope, intention and fact are different levels of commitment.
grammarFocus: Focus a past event with 是…的
Give a reason with 因為…所以…

title: After class means after class
setup: Two friends arrange a birthday visit around a language exchange. Find the actual meeting trigger and place.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 好久不見！明天是你的生日，對不對？
lines.pinyin: Hǎojiǔ bú jiàn! Míngtiān shì nǐ de shēngrì, duì bú duì?
lines.translation: Long time no see! Tomorrow is your birthday, right?
lines.note: The greeting establishes a reunion. 對不對 asks for confirmation of the birthday date, rather than introducing a choice between two dates.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 對，你還記得！我明天下午有語言交換。
lines.pinyin: Duì, nǐ hái jìde! Wǒ míngtiān xiàwǔ yǒu yǔyán jiāohuàn.
lines.translation: Yes, you still remember! I have a language exchange tomorrow afternoon.
lines.note: 還記得 expresses continued memory. The afternoon exchange is a separate commitment that the birthday visit must fit around.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 跟誰？是那個很熱心的朋友嗎？
lines.pinyin: Gēn shéi? Shì nà ge hěn rèxīn de péngyǒu ma?
lines.translation: With whom? Is it that very helpful friend?
lines.note: 跟誰 asks for the companion. 很熱心的 identifies a person by a known quality, not by a new name the learner must decode.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 對。他教我西班牙文，我教他中文。
lines.pinyin: Duì. Tā jiāo wǒ Xībānyáwén, wǒ jiāo tā Zhōngwén.
lines.translation: Yes. He teaches me Spanish, and I teach him Chinese.
lines.note: Each clause reverses teacher and learner. Follow the subject before 教 to avoid swapping who teaches which language.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 那我們什麼時候見面？我四點左右有空。
lines.pinyin: Nà wǒmen shénme shíhòu jiànmiàn? Wǒ sì diǎn zuǒyòu yǒukòng.
lines.translation: Then when shall we meet? I’m free around four.
lines.note: 左右 makes four o’clock approximate. This describes Lin’s availability, not yet the exact time of their joint meeting.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 我三點半有課，四點半下課。我一下課就去找你。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ sān diǎn bàn yǒu kè, sì diǎn bàn xiàkè. Wǒ yí xiàkè jiù qù zhǎo nǐ.
lines.translation: I have class at three thirty and finish at four thirty. I’ll come find you as soon as class ends.
lines.note: 一…就… links the visit immediately to the end of class. It overrides any assumption that being free around four guarantees a four o’clock meeting.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 好，我在圖書館門口等你。我們先喝茶，再吃飯。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ zài túshūguǎn ménkǒu děng nǐ. Wǒmen xiān hē chá, zài chīfàn.
lines.translation: Okay, I’ll wait at the library entrance. We’ll have tea first and then eat.
lines.note: 門口 fixes the meeting point at the entrance, not inside. 先…再… orders two shared activities after they meet.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 太好了！我也很想和你一起吃飯。
lines.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Wǒ yě hěn xiǎng hé nǐ yìqǐ chīfàn.
lines.translation: Great! I’m really looking forward to eating with you too.
lines.note: The enthusiastic response accepts the arrangement and expresses a shared wish. It does not move the meeting to an earlier time.

questions.prompt: What triggers Mei’s visit?
options: The start of the language exchange
questions.explanation: Mei says she will go as soon as class ends, and explicitly places that end at four thirty.

questions.prompt: Who teaches Spanish in the exchange?
questions.explanation: The friend is the subject of 他教我西班牙文, while Mei teaches Chinese in return.

questions.prompt: Where and in what activity order will they meet?
questions.explanation: The agreed entrance and the 先…再… sequence together identify the correct arrangement.

questions.prompt: Why is “exactly four o’clock” not a good summary?
options: Lin gives an approximate time and Mei finishes later
questions.explanation: 左右 makes Lin’s time approximate, while Mei’s class ends at four thirty and the visit follows that event.

tips: An event trigger can determine a plan more precisely than someone’s approximate availability.
In reciprocal exchanges, re-check the subject of each clause rather than assuming one person is always the teacher.
grammarFocus: As soon as… with 一…就…
Tell clock time with 點 and 分

title: Birthday dinner: ordered or only suggested?
setup: Read a birthday group chat. Distinguish what is already ordered, what someone will bring, and what is only proposed.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 明天是Mei的生日。我訂了豬腳麵線，也訂了蛋糕。
lines.pinyin: Míngtiān shì Mei de shēngrì. Wǒ dìng le zhūjiǎo miànxiàn, yě dìng le dàngāo.
lines.translation: Tomorrow is Mei’s birthday. I’ve ordered pork-knuckle noodles and a cake.
lines.note: 了 after 訂 marks completed ordering. The food may be eaten tomorrow even though the order has already been placed.

lines.speaker: Chen
lines.text: 你是不是也訂了牛肉麵？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ shì bú shì yě dìng le niúròu miàn?
lines.translation: Did you also order beef noodles?
lines.note: 是不是 requests confirmation of a possible additional order. The question itself is not evidence that beef noodles are included.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 沒有，我沒訂牛肉麵。Mei什麼都吃，可是她最喜歡麵線。
lines.pinyin: Méiyǒu, wǒ méi dìng niúròu miàn. Mei shénme dōu chī, kěshì tā zuì xǐhuān miànxiàn.
lines.translation: No, I didn’t order beef noodles. Mei eats everything, but her favorite is thin noodles.
lines.note: 沒 negates a completed action without retaining verbal 了. 什麼都 expresses an inclusive range, while 最 still allows a favorite within it.

lines.speaker: Chen
lines.text: 我買了一本書，明天給她。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū, míngtiān gěi tā.
lines.translation: I bought a book; I’ll give it to her tomorrow.
lines.note: The purchase is completed, but the giving is scheduled for tomorrow. Keep the two actions and their times separate.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 謝謝你們！你們跟我的家人一樣，都很熱心。
lines.pinyin: Xièxie nǐmen! Nǐmen gēn wǒ de jiārén yíyàng, dōu hěn rèxīn.
lines.translation: Thank you! You’re like my family—both so helpful.
lines.note: 跟…一樣 compares the friends with Mei’s family, and 都很熱心 specifies the shared quality. It does not claim the friends are relatives.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 不必客氣。明天晚上六點在我家吃飯。
lines.pinyin: Bú bì kèqì. Míngtiān wǎnshang liù diǎn zài wǒ jiā chīfàn.
lines.translation: You’re welcome. Dinner is at my home at six tomorrow evening.
lines.note: Time precedes location and the meal action. The speaker’s 我家 identifies Lin’s home rather than Mei’s or Chen’s.

lines.speaker: Chen
lines.text: 吃飯以後，我們唱歌，好不好？
lines.pinyin: Chīfàn yǐhòu, wǒmen chànggē, hǎo bù hǎo?
lines.translation: Shall we sing after dinner?
lines.note: 以後 places the proposed activity after eating. 好不好 seeks agreement; no following message explicitly accepts the singing plan.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: Mei，祝你生日快樂，心想事成！
lines.pinyin: Mei, zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè, xīn xiǎng shì chéng!
lines.translation: Mei, happy birthday! May your wishes come true!
lines.note: 祝 introduces wishes directed to the recipient. A birthday wish closes the chat warmly but does not answer every earlier planning question.

questions.prompt: Which items has Lin already ordered?
questions.explanation: Lin explicitly names the two completed orders and denies ordering beef noodles.

questions.prompt: Which part of Chen’s gift plan is already completed?
questions.explanation: 買了 marks the purchase as completed; 明天 places giving the book in the future.

questions.prompt: At whose home is dinner?
questions.explanation: Lin is the speaker who says 我家, so the home belongs to Lin in the conversation.

questions.prompt: Which activity remains a proposal without an explicit acceptance?
questions.explanation: Chen proposes singing with 好不好. The final birthday wish does not explicitly confirm that proposal.

tips: An action can be completed before a future celebration: ordering today and eating tomorrow are compatible.
Resolve “my home” from the speaker label, and distinguish warm replies from explicit acceptance of a plan.
grammarFocus: All-inclusive question words with 都 / 也

title: The weather update changes the outing
setup: Read a weather note and the conversation it prompts. Compare today with yesterday, then identify the group’s final plan.

lines.speaker: Weather note
lines.text: 今天有颱風。風比昨天更大，雨也很大。
lines.pinyin: Jīntiān yǒu táifēng. Fēng bǐ zuótiān gèng dà, yǔ yě hěn dà.
lines.translation: There is a typhoon today. The wind is even stronger than yesterday, and the rain is heavy too.
lines.note: 比 sets yesterday as the comparison baseline. 更 emphasizes a further increase; the rain is described as heavy without an explicit yesterday comparison.

lines.speaker: Weather note
lines.text: 今天沒有昨天那麼冷，可是外面很濕。
lines.pinyin: Jīntiān méiyǒu zuótiān nàme lěng, kěshì wàimiàn hěn shī.
lines.translation: Today is not as cold as yesterday, but it is very wet outside.
lines.note: 沒有…那麼… expresses a lower degree of cold. Milder temperature does not mean weaker wind or better conditions overall.

lines.speaker: Lin · message
lines.text: 我們今天還去山上看風景嗎？
lines.pinyin: Wǒmen jīntiān hái qù shānshàng kàn fēngjǐng ma?
lines.translation: Are we still going up the mountain to see the scenery today?
lines.note: 還 asks whether a previous plan remains in effect. Asking about the trip is not the same as confirming that it will happen.

lines.speaker: Mei · reply
lines.text: 不去了。我覺得這次颱風比上次更可怕。
lines.pinyin: Bú qù le. Wǒ juéde zhè cì táifēng bǐ shàng cì gèng kěpà.
lines.translation: We’re not going now. I think this typhoon is even scarier than the last one.
lines.note: Sentence-final 了 signals a changed plan. 我覺得 frames the comparison as Mei’s assessment, not a numerical weather measurement.

lines.speaker: Lin · message
lines.text: 那我們在家看電影吧。我有一部很好看的電影。
lines.pinyin: Nà wǒmen zài jiā kàn diànyǐng ba. Wǒ yǒu yí bù hěn hǎokàn de diànyǐng.
lines.translation: Then let’s watch a movie at home. I have a very good movie.
lines.note: 那 connects an alternative to the cancellation. 在家 changes the location of the activity, rather than finding another outdoor destination.

lines.speaker: Mei · reply
lines.text: 好啊。我先看新聞，再跟你看電影。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo a. Wǒ xiān kàn xīnwén, zài gēn nǐ kàn diànyǐng.
lines.translation: Sure. I’ll watch the news first, then watch the movie with you.
lines.note: 好啊 accepts the indoor activity. 先…再… adds an order to the activities without reversing the cancellation of the mountain trip.

lines.speaker: Lin · message
lines.text: 雨要停了嗎？
lines.pinyin: Yǔ yào tíng le ma?
lines.translation: Is the rain about to stop?
lines.note: 要…了 asks about an imminent change. Because this is a question, it does not establish that the rain is actually stopping.

lines.speaker: Mei · reply
lines.text: 我不知道。要是你出去，一定要小心。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhīdào. Yàoshi nǐ chūqù, yídìng yào xiǎoxīn.
lines.translation: I don’t know. If you go out, be sure to be careful.
lines.note: The reply leaves the weather change unknown. 要是 introduces a conditional warning, not a new agreement to go outdoors together.

questions.prompt: Compared with yesterday, what is stated about today?
questions.explanation: The wind comparison says stronger, while the temperature comparison says not as cold. These are different dimensions.

questions.prompt: What is the agreed replacement activity?
options: Watching a movie at home after the news
questions.explanation: Mei cancels the trip and accepts the movie plan, adding that she will watch the news first.

questions.prompt: Do they know the rain is about to stop?
options: No; the question receives “I don’t know”
No; they know it will never stop
questions.explanation: The question is explicitly answered with uncertainty. It cannot be used as evidence for an imminent weather change.

questions.prompt: Which statement is specifically Mei’s personal comparison?
options: This typhoon feels scarier than the last
questions.explanation: 我覺得 marks Mei’s assessment of this typhoon compared with the previous one.

tips: Compare one property at a time: less cold can coexist with stronger wind.
Do not turn a question about what might happen into a forecast that it will happen.
grammarFocus: Condition and consequence with 要是…就…

部.note: Reading-only support for counting one film.

電影.note: The movie noun from the already-taught expression 看電影, to watch a movie.

title: A friend offers to come along
setup: Read a conversation about feeling ill. This is language practice: follow the reported symptoms and the offer of help, not medical advice.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 你怎麼了？臉色不太好看。
lines.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme le? Liǎnsè bú tài hǎokàn.
lines.translation: What’s wrong? You don’t look very well.
lines.note: 怎麼了 asks about a problem or changed situation. The observation concerns appearance and does not by itself establish a diagnosis.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 我昨天晚上肚子痛，吐了兩次。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān wǎnshang dùzi tòng, tù le liǎng cì.
lines.translation: My stomach hurt last night, and I vomited twice.
lines.note: 昨天晚上 supplies the time. 次 counts occurrences of vomiting, not the number of days the person has been ill.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 今天還痛嗎？你有沒有發燒？
lines.pinyin: Jīntiān hái tòng ma? Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu fāshāo?
lines.translation: Does it still hurt today? Do you have a fever?
lines.note: 還 asks whether the earlier symptom continues. The second question asks about another symptom without asserting that it is present.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 今天還有一點痛，沒有發燒。我沒吃什麼東西。
lines.pinyin: Jīntiān hái yǒuyìdiǎn tòng, méiyǒu fāshāo. Wǒ méi chī shénme dōngxi.
lines.translation: It still hurts a little today, but I don’t have a fever. I haven’t eaten much.
lines.note: In a negative statement, 沒吃什麼東西 means not eating much or anything substantial; 什麼 is not asking the reader to name a food.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 你去看醫生了嗎？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ qù kàn yīshēng le ma?
lines.translation: Have you been to see a doctor?
lines.note: The question checks whether a visit has happened. It must be read together with the reply rather than assumed to confirm an earlier visit.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 還沒有。我有健康保險，等一下就去健康中心。
lines.pinyin: Hái méiyǒu. Wǒ yǒu jiànkāng bǎoxiǎn, děng yíxià jiù qù jiànkāng zhōngxīn.
lines.translation: Not yet. I have health insurance, and I’ll go to the health center shortly.
lines.note: 還沒有 denies a completed visit. 等一下就 presents going to the health center as a near-future plan, not something that has already happened.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 我陪你去。你看了醫生就跟我去拿藥，好不好？
lines.pinyin: Wǒ péi nǐ qù. Nǐ kàn le yīshēng jiù gēn wǒ qù ná yào, hǎo bù hǎo?
lines.translation: I’ll go with you. After you’ve seen the doctor, shall we go get medicine together?
lines.note: V了…就… sequences a proposed next action after the first is completed. Here 了 does not mean the doctor visit has already happened.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 謝謝。我的朋友等一下來，他陪我去。你不用陪我。
lines.pinyin: Xièxie. Wǒ de péngyǒu děng yíxià lái, tā péi wǒ qù. Nǐ bú yòng péi wǒ.
lines.translation: Thanks. My friend is coming shortly and will go with me. You don’t need to come along.
lines.note: Lin gives a reason for declining Mei’s offer: another friend will accompany him. The refusal concerns the companion, not whether to seek help.

questions.prompt: What happened twice?
questions.explanation: 兩次 counts the vomiting episodes. No completed doctor visits or medicine doses are counted in the passage.

questions.prompt: Which description matches Lin today?
options: Some stomach pain, no fever, little food
No symptoms and a large lunch
questions.explanation: Lin’s reply says there is still some pain, denies fever and states that he has eaten little.

questions.prompt: Has Lin already seen a doctor?
options: The passage says he never will
No; he says “not yet” and plans to go
questions.explanation: 還沒有 directly answers the visit question. The proposed sequence in the next line is not proof of a completed visit.

questions.prompt: Why does Lin decline Mei’s company?
options: Another friend is coming to accompany him
He is already at the pharmacy
questions.explanation: Lin says another friend will accompany him, so Mei’s help is unnecessary. He does not cancel the health-center plan.

tips: Separate a symptom report from a question and from a diagnosis the passage never provides.
In a future sequence, V了…就… can describe what will happen after completing an action, not what has already happened.
grammarFocus: V了…就… — do B right after completing A

title: One order, two prices
setup: Read a small drink-order card. Use both the quantities and the prices.

lines.speaker: Price card
lines.text: 熱茶一杯二十塊，熱咖啡一杯四十塊。
lines.pinyin: Rè chá yì bēi èrshí kuài, rè kāfēi yì bēi sìshí kuài.
lines.translation: Hot tea is twenty dollars a cup; hot coffee is forty dollars a cup.
lines.note: Each 一杯 gives the price for one cup. The two prices belong to different drinks, not to two sizes of the same drink.

lines.speaker: Order
lines.text: 我要兩杯熱茶，一杯熱咖啡。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ yào liǎng bēi rè chá, yì bēi rè kāfēi.
lines.translation: I’d like two hot teas and one hot coffee.
lines.note: 兩杯 counts the teas, while 一杯 counts the coffee. Keep those quantities with the correct prices on the card.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: 都外帶。一共多少錢？
lines.pinyin: Dōu wàidài. Yígòng duōshǎo qián?
lines.translation: All to go. How much altogether?
lines.note: 都 covers all three cups from the order. 一共 asks for the total, not the price of just the final cup.

lines.speaker: Staff
lines.text: 一共八十塊。謝謝！
lines.pinyin: Yígòng bāshí kuài. Xièxie!
lines.translation: Eighty dollars altogether. Thank you!
lines.note: Two teas cost forty, and one coffee costs another forty. The total therefore agrees with the prices and quantities above.

questions.prompt: Which calculation matches the order?
questions.explanation: There are two twenty-dollar teas and one forty-dollar coffee, giving the stated eighty-dollar total.

questions.prompt: Which drinks are to go?
questions.explanation: 都 applies to the entire preceding order: the two teas and the coffee are all takeout.

tips: Match each quantity to its item before calculating.
Scope words such as 都 can apply to several items named earlier.

title: The noodle-shop order slip
setup: Read an order slip and the customer’s comment. Distinguish quantities from opinions.

lines.speaker: Order
lines.text: 牛肉麵兩碗，湯一碗。
lines.pinyin: Niúròu miàn liǎng wǎn, tāng yì wǎn.
lines.translation: Two bowls of beef noodles and one bowl of soup.
lines.note: Order slips can put the item before its quantity. 碗 counts bowls for both items, but their quantities are different.

lines.speaker: Service
lines.text: 內用，不外帶。
lines.pinyin: Nèiyòng, bú wàidài.
lines.translation: For here, not to go.
lines.note: The service line applies to the whole order. It does not change the food or the number of bowls listed above.

lines.speaker: Customer
lines.text: 我最喜歡這家店的牛肉麵，真好吃！
lines.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuān zhè jiā diàn de niúròu miàn, zhēn hǎochī!
lines.translation: This shop’s beef noodles are my favorite. They’re really delicious!
lines.note: 最 identifies the customer’s strongest preference. 真好吃 is an opinion about taste, not a statement about price.

lines.speaker: Companion
lines.text: 我也喜歡牛肉麵。今天我想喝湯。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ yě xǐhuān niúròu miàn. Jīntiān wǒ xiǎng hē tāng.
lines.translation: I like beef noodles too. Today I feel like soup.
lines.note: The companion separates a general preference from today’s choice. This contrast does not remove the noodles already on the slip.

questions.prompt: How many bowls are listed altogether?
questions.explanation: The slip lists two bowls of noodles plus one bowl of soup, so the total is three bowls.

questions.prompt: What does the customer’s comment establish?
options: The noodles are the customer’s favorite
questions.explanation: 最喜歡 identifies a favorite. The comment gives no price comparison, and the service line says for here.

tips: A slip often omits full sentence wording; item and quantity still stay paired.
A favorite food is a preference, not evidence about its price.
grammarFocus: Drink the broth; react to the taste

title: Where is everyone now?
setup: Read a short exchange during class time. Follow the correction and the two different people.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 你現在在學校外面嗎？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ xiànzài zài xuéxiào wàimiàn ma?
lines.translation: Are you outside the school now?
lines.note: 現在 asks about current whereabouts. Because the location appears in a question, it is not yet an established fact.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 不，我在圖書館裡面看書。
lines.pinyin: Bù, wǒ zài túshūguǎn lǐmiàn kàn shū.
lines.translation: No, I’m reading inside the library.
lines.note: 不 rejects the suggested location. 在圖書館裡面 comes before 看書 to place the reading activity inside the library.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 你姐姐也在那裡嗎？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ jiějie yě zài nàlǐ ma?
lines.translation: Is your older sister there too?
lines.note: 那裡 points back to the library. 也 asks whether the sister shares Mei’s location, rather than asserting that she does.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 她不在圖書館，她在學校上課。
lines.pinyin: Tā bú zài túshūguǎn, tā zài xuéxiào shàngkè.
lines.translation: She isn’t in the library; she’s having class at school.
lines.note: 不在 denies one location, and the second clause gives the sister’s activity. Mei and her sister are doing different things.

questions.prompt: Who is reading in the library?
questions.explanation: Mei says she is reading there, while her sister is specifically said not to be in the library.

questions.prompt: What does “there” in Lin’s second message refer to?
questions.explanation: The immediately preceding answer establishes the library as the location that 那裡 refers back to.

tips: Do not treat a location question as a fact.
Resolve “there” from the last established location.
grammarFocus: Put now before the location statement
Negate a location with 不在

title: The free hour is not the whole afternoon
setup: Read a short availability note and a reply. Find a meeting time inside the stated window.

lines.speaker: Mei · availability
lines.text: 明天從中午十二點到一點，我有空。
lines.pinyin: Míngtiān cóng zhōngwǔ shí’èr diǎn dào yì diǎn, wǒ yǒukòng.
lines.translation: Tomorrow I’m free from noon until one.
lines.note: 從…到… gives both boundaries of availability. It does not say that Mei is free throughout the rest of the day.

lines.speaker: Mei · location
lines.text: 我在學校附近。我們在圖書館外面見面吧。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ zài xuéxiào fùjìn. Wǒmen zài túshūguǎn wàimiàn jiànmiàn ba.
lines.translation: I’ll be near school. Let’s meet outside the library.
lines.note: The first clause gives a broad area; the second proposes a more precise meeting point outside, rather than inside, the library.

lines.speaker: Lin · proposal
lines.text: 十二點二十分見面，好不好？
lines.pinyin: Shí’èr diǎn èrshí fēn jiànmiàn, hǎo bù hǎo?
lines.translation: Shall we meet at twelve twenty?
lines.note: The hour comes before 點 and the minutes before 分. This time falls within Mei’s stated noon-to-one window.

lines.speaker: Mei · reply
lines.text: 沒問題。一點我要去上課。
lines.pinyin: Méi wèntí. Yì diǎn wǒ yào qù shàngkè.
lines.translation: No problem. At one I need to go to class.
lines.note: The reply accepts the proposed time and explains the end of the free window. Going to class limits how long the meeting can continue.

questions.prompt: Which appointment is accepted?
questions.explanation: The place comes from Mei’s proposal, the time from Lin’s reply, and 沒問題 confirms their combination.

questions.prompt: Why should they not assume Mei is free after one?
options: Mei needs to go to class
questions.explanation: The window ends at one, and the last message gives class as the reason for that boundary.

tips: Combine the time from one message with the place from another.
Check both ends of an availability window.
grammarFocus: Tell clock time with 點 and 分
Mark a range with 從…到…

title: A faster train, a different choice
setup: Two friends compare travel choices. A favorable description does not always tell you what they choose.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 明天你跟誰去玩？
lines.pinyin: Míngtiān nǐ gēn shéi qù wán?
lines.translation: Who are you going out with tomorrow?
lines.note: 跟誰 asks about a companion. The time is tomorrow, so this is a plan rather than a completed trip.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 我跟姐姐去。我們想坐火車。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ gēn jiějie qù. Wǒmen xiǎng zuò huǒchē.
lines.translation: I’m going with my older sister. We want to take the train.
lines.note: The first sentence answers who, and the second gives their transport preference. 姐姐 is the companion, not the destination.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 高鐵比較快，又快又舒服。
lines.pinyin: Gāotiě bǐjiào kuài, yòu kuài yòu shūfu.
lines.translation: High-speed rail is faster; it’s both fast and comfortable.
lines.note: 比較 makes a contextual comparison, and 又…又… joins two favorable qualities. Lin has not yet changed Mei’s stated choice.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 我知道，可是姐姐覺得高鐵車票太貴了。我們坐火車吧。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào, kěshì jiějie juéde gāotiě chēpiào tài guì le. Wǒmen zuò huǒchē ba.
lines.translation: I know, but my sister thinks high-speed rail tickets are too expensive. Let’s take the regular train.
lines.note: 可是 introduces the competing concern: price. The final suggestion keeps the regular train despite the high-speed option’s advantages.

questions.prompt: Why does Mei still favor the regular train?
options: The faster option is considered too expensive
questions.explanation: The fast, comfortable option loses out because the sister considers its ticket too expensive.

questions.prompt: Who is Mei planning to travel with?
questions.explanation: Mei directly answers the companion question with 跟姐姐去. Lin discusses the plan but is not named as her companion.

tips: Separate the best-described option from the option actually chosen.
A transport comparison and a companion question ask for different information.
grammarFocus: Both A and B with 又…又…

title: A recommendation is not a decision
setup: Read a brief holiday-planning chat. Notice the difference between someone’s plan and a friend’s advice.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 放假的時候，我打算去玩兩個星期。
lines.pinyin: Fàngjià de shíhòu, wǒ dǎsuàn qù wán liǎng ge xīngqí.
lines.translation: During the holiday, I plan to go away for two weeks.
lines.note: 的時候 locates the activity during a holiday. 兩個星期 follows the activity to state its duration rather than the date it begins.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 你應該去夜市。那裡的小吃很特別。
lines.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi qù yèshì. Nàlǐ de xiǎochī hěn tèbié.
lines.translation: You should visit the night market. The snacks there are special.
lines.note: 應該 gives advice here. The description explains Lin’s recommendation without proving that Mei has agreed to follow it.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 我有時候喜歡去商店，有時候喜歡在茶館喝茶。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ yǒushíhòu xǐhuān qù shāngdiàn, yǒushíhòu xǐhuān zài cháguǎn hē chá.
lines.translation: Sometimes I like going to shops; sometimes I like having tea at a tea house.
lines.note: 有時候…有時候… describes alternate preferences across occasions. It does not schedule both activities on particular days of this trip.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 我沒有決定去哪裡。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu juédìng qù nǎlǐ.
lines.translation: I haven’t decided where to go yet.
lines.note: The final statement leaves the destination unsettled. It does not cancel the earlier two-week intention or turn the advice into a booking.

questions.prompt: Which part of the plan is stated, even though the destination is undecided?
questions.explanation: Mei gives a two-week duration but explicitly says the destination has not yet been decided.

questions.prompt: What role does the night market play?
options: A place Mei refuses to visit
The place they are currently in
questions.explanation: Lin recommends it with 應該, but Mei’s final message makes clear she has not settled on a destination.

tips: A stated duration can coexist with an undecided destination.
Advice is not confirmation that the listener will follow it.
grammarFocus: Say how long with a duration after the verb
Give a suggestion with 應該
Alternate possibilities with 有時候…有時候…

title: A photo and a guess
setup: Read a photo caption and two comments. Work out which claim the reply confirms.

lines.speaker: Caption
lines.text: 今天和朋友一起吃水果。芒果黃黃的，很香。
lines.pinyin: Jīntiān hé péngyǒu yìqǐ chī shuǐguǒ. Mángguǒ huánghuáng de, hěn xiāng.
lines.translation: Eating fruit with a friend today. The mango is yellow and fragrant.
lines.note: A caption can omit an understood subject. 黃黃的 presents a descriptive impression of the mango rather than a color comparison.

lines.speaker: Lin · comment
lines.text: 你今天穿紅色衣服吧？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān chuān hóngsè yīfu ba?
lines.translation: You’re wearing red today, right?
lines.note: 吧 marks a guess offered for confirmation. The guess concerns the person’s clothing today, not the color of the fruit.

lines.speaker: Mei · reply
lines.text: 對！我很開心，朋友給我照相。
lines.pinyin: Duì! Wǒ hěn kāixīn, péngyǒu gěi wǒ zhàoxiàng.
lines.translation: Right! I’m very happy; my friend is taking a photo of me.
lines.note: 對 confirms Lin’s identification. The friend is the photographer, while 我 is the person receiving that help.

lines.speaker: Mei · reply
lines.text: 這個芒果很甜，你也吃吃看。
lines.pinyin: Zhè ge mángguǒ hěn tián, nǐ yě chīchīkàn.
lines.translation: This mango is sweet; you should try some too.
lines.note: 吃吃看 invites someone to try the food. The 看 in this pattern adds trying, rather than asking someone merely to look at the mango.

questions.prompt: Who is identified as wearing red?
questions.explanation: Lin guesses that the person in red is Mei, and Mei answers 對 to confirm it.

questions.prompt: What does Mei invite Lin to do?
questions.explanation: 吃吃看 means to try eating it. It is not an instruction simply to look at the fruit.

tips: Wait for the reply before treating a guess as confirmed.
Read VV看 as a whole try-it pattern.
grammarFocus: Use 吧 to make a guess
Give a subjective impression by reduplicating a state verb

title: The rent call has one loose end
setup: Read a tenant–landlord exchange. One payment is confirmed, but a problem remains.

lines.speaker: Tenant
lines.text: 喂，房東，你收到房租了嗎？
lines.pinyin: Wéi, fángdōng, nǐ shōudào fángzū le ma?
lines.translation: Hello, landlord—have you received the rent?
lines.note: 喂 opens a telephone-style exchange. The question checks receipt of the rent, not whether the tenant likes the room.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.text: 收到了，謝謝。住在這裡習慣了嗎？
lines.pinyin: Shōudào le, xièxie. Zhù zài zhèlǐ xíguàn le ma?
lines.translation: Yes, thank you. Have you got used to living here?
lines.note: 收到了 leaves the understood rent unspoken. The following question shifts from payment to becoming accustomed to the home.

lines.speaker: Tenant
lines.text: 習慣了，不過熱水器好像有問題。
lines.pinyin: Xíguàn le, búguò rèshuǐqì hǎoxiàng yǒu wèntí.
lines.translation: Yes, but there seems to be a problem with the water heater.
lines.note: 不過 introduces a qualification to the positive answer. 好像 makes the problem tentative rather than a precise technical diagnosis.

lines.speaker: Landlord
lines.text: 不好意思。我明天來看看。
lines.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi. Wǒ míngtiān lái kànkan.
lines.translation: Sorry about that. I’ll come take a look tomorrow.
lines.note: 明天 places the visit in the future. Offering to inspect the heater is not a claim that the problem has already been fixed.

questions.prompt: Which matter is confirmed as completed?
questions.explanation: The landlord directly confirms receiving the rent. The heater visit is still planned for tomorrow.

questions.prompt: What is the promised next action?
options: Come look at the heater tomorrow
questions.explanation: The tenant raises a possible heater problem, and the landlord promises to come look tomorrow, without promising a specific repair.

tips: Recover omitted objects from the previous question.
An inspection promised for tomorrow is not a repair completed today.
grammarFocus: Introduce an indefinite subject with 有
Leave understood subjects and objects unspoken

title: Study first, then look for work
setup: Read a short personal plan. Distinguish the sequence from assumptions about how easy it will be.

lines.speaker: Plan
lines.text: 我想先念書，再找工作。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiān niànshū, zài zhǎo gōngzuò.
lines.translation: I want to study first, then look for work.
lines.note: 先…再… places the two activities in order. Looking for work is a future intention, not evidence that a job has already been found.

lines.speaker: Reason
lines.text: 我希望在這個國家上班，可是工作不好找。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng zài zhè ge guójiā shàngbān, kěshì gōngzuò bù hǎo zhǎo.
lines.translation: I hope to work in this country, but jobs are not easy to find.
lines.note: 不好找 describes difficulty finding work. It does not mean the jobs themselves are morally bad or necessarily unpleasant.

lines.speaker: Next step
lines.text: 念一年中文以後，我想試試。
lines.pinyin: Niàn yì nián Zhōngwén yǐhòu, wǒ xiǎng shìshi.
lines.translation: After studying Chinese for a year, I’d like to give it a try.
lines.note: 以後 makes a year of study the earlier event and trying the later one. The understood thing to try is the job search from the preceding lines.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: 加油！我也覺得學中文很有意思。
lines.pinyin: Jiāyóu! Wǒ yě juéde xué Zhōngwén hěn yǒuyìsi.
lines.translation: Keep going! I also find learning Chinese interesting.
lines.note: 加油 encourages the plan. Enjoying Chinese is supportive, but the friend does not guarantee that finding a job will be easy.

questions.prompt: What does 不好找 mean here?
options: The country has no jobs at all
questions.explanation: 好 or 不好 before 找 evaluates how easy finding something is; it does not evaluate the quality of the job itself.

questions.prompt: Which sequence matches the plan?
options: Start a job, then learn Chinese
Study Chinese, then try looking for work
questions.explanation: Both the first-then statement and the 以後 statement place Chinese study before trying the job search.

tips: Read 好/不好 + verb as an ease judgment when the taught pattern applies.
Encouragement supports an intention without guaranteeing its result.
grammarFocus: Special meanings of 好 / 難 + verbs

title: A gift bought, a meal not ordered
setup: Read a birthday-planning exchange. Keep buying and ordering separate.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 我買了禮物。你訂了豬腳麵線嗎？
lines.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le lǐwù. Nǐ dìng le zhūjiǎo miànxiàn ma?
lines.translation: I bought a gift. Have you ordered pork-knuckle noodles?
lines.note: The first 了 marks a completed purchase. The second appears in a question, so it does not confirm a completed food order.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 還沒訂。我今天晚上訂。
lines.pinyin: Hái méi dìng. Wǒ jīntiān wǎnshang dìng.
lines.translation: Not yet. I’ll order tonight.
lines.note: 沒訂 denies completion and does not keep verbal 了. The following time expression moves the ordering to a plan for this evening.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 好，我們明天一起吃飯。我想吃一點麵線。
lines.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒmen míngtiān yìqǐ chīfàn. Wǒ xiǎng chī yìdiǎn miànxiàn.
lines.translation: Okay, we’ll eat together tomorrow. I’d like a little thin-noodle dish.
lines.note: 明天 dates the meal rather than the ordering. 一點 before the food is a small quantity here, not the clock time one o’clock.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 沒問題。禮物是什麼？
lines.pinyin: Méi wèntí. Lǐwù shì shénme?
lines.translation: No problem. What is the gift?
lines.note: The final question asks about the already-bought gift. Since no answer follows, its exact identity remains unknown to the reader.

questions.prompt: Which action is already completed?
questions.explanation: Lin states 買了禮物, while Mei explicitly says the noodles have not yet been ordered.

questions.prompt: What information is still missing?
questions.explanation: Ordering time, meal time and Lin’s food preference are stated, but the gift question receives no answer.

tips: A positive completed action and a question about another action carry different evidence.
Check whether 一點 is followed by a food or used as a clock time.

title: Two seasons, two different activities
setup: Read two friends’ seasonal notes. Weather preferences explain why their plans differ.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 冬天很冷，可是我喜歡冬天。
lines.pinyin: Dōngtiān hěn lěng, kěshì wǒ xǐhuān dōngtiān.
lines.translation: Winter is cold, but I like winter.
lines.note: 可是 contrasts the cold weather with a positive preference. Cold does not automatically mean the speaker dislikes the season.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 山上下雪的時候，我想去滑雪。
lines.pinyin: Shānshàng xiàxuě de shíhòu, wǒ xiǎng qù huáxuě.
lines.translation: When it snows in the mountains, I want to go skiing.
lines.note: 的時候 connects the intended activity to snowy conditions. 想 makes skiing a wish rather than a report of an already-completed trip.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 我不喜歡冷的天氣。我最喜歡夏天。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuān lěng de tiānqì. Wǒ zuì xǐhuān xiàtiān.
lines.translation: I don’t like cold weather. Summer is my favorite.
lines.note: The speaker has changed, so this preference belongs to Lin rather than contradicting Mei’s winter preference.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 因為我喜歡游泳，所以夏天常和朋友去游泳池。
lines.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ xǐhuān yóuyǒng, suǒyǐ xiàtiān cháng hé péngyǒu qù yóuyǒngchí.
lines.translation: Because I like swimming, I often go to the pool with friends in summer.
lines.note: 因為 introduces the reason and 所以 the habitual result. 常 describes frequency rather than a single appointment at a fixed time.

questions.prompt: Which pairing fits the two writers?
options: Mei: summer swimming; Lin: winter skiing
Mei: winter skiing; Lin: summer swimming
Both plan a mountain trip tomorrow
questions.explanation: Mei’s winter preference connects to skiing, while Lin’s summer preference connects to swimming.

questions.prompt: Is Mei reporting a ski trip that already happened?
options: No; she expresses a wish for snowy conditions
questions.explanation: The line uses 想 and a when-it-snows condition. It gives no completed ski trip or past date.

tips: Keep each preference attached to its speaker.
Separate a seasonal habit from a wish and from a completed event.
grammarFocus: Give a reason with 因為…所以…

title: Yesterday’s cold, today’s symptoms
setup: Read a short symptom report. This is a comprehension exercise; the passage does not give a diagnosis.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 你今天怎麼樣？昨天天氣很冷。
lines.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān zěnmeyàng? Zuótiān tiānqì hěn lěng.
lines.translation: How are you today? The weather was cold yesterday.
lines.note: 今天 asks about the person now, while 昨天 describes earlier weather. The weather comment alone does not establish a cause of illness.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 我今天一直流鼻水，頭也很痛。
lines.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yìzhí liú bíshuǐ, tóu yě hěn tòng.
lines.translation: My nose keeps running today, and my head really hurts too.
lines.note: 一直 presents the runny nose as continuing. 也 adds a second symptom, so the headache is not the only reported problem.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.text: 你有沒有發燒？胃口怎麼樣？
lines.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu méiyǒu fāshāo? Wèikǒu zěnmeyàng?
lines.translation: Do you have a fever? How is your appetite?
lines.note: The first sentence asks whether fever is present, and the second asks about appetite. Neither question supplies its own answer.

lines.speaker: Lin
lines.text: 沒有發燒，可是胃口很差。我想去看醫生。
lines.pinyin: Méiyǒu fāshāo, kěshì wèikǒu hěn chà. Wǒ xiǎng qù kàn yīshēng.
lines.translation: I don’t have a fever, but my appetite is poor. I want to see a doctor.
lines.note: 沒有 denies fever, while 可是 introduces a different problem. 想去 makes the doctor visit an intention, not a completed visit or diagnosis.

questions.prompt: Which symptom does Lin explicitly deny?
questions.explanation: Lin reports the runny nose, headache and poor appetite, but directly says there is no fever.

questions.prompt: What can we conclude about seeing a doctor?
options: Lin wants to go, but no completed visit is stated
questions.explanation: Lin expresses a wish to see a doctor. The passage does not report that a visit or diagnosis has already happened.

tips: Keep reported symptoms separate from symptoms mentioned only in questions.
An intention to seek help does not tell you the outcome of a visit.
